subject: Post-call: Slim log / short-retention options and next steps
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.ai>
To: Lara Mitchell <lara@cloudverahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-29T09:12:00Z
Subject: Post-call: Slim log / short-retention options and next steps

Hi Lara — thanks again for the quick call this morning. Wanted to capture the main points and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned.

Recap of what we heard from CloudVera:  
- Primary ask: minimize persistence of any PII or PHI that touches inference requests; preference for 0-retention on model inputs where possible.  
- If 0-retention isn’t achievable for some workflows, customer is open to a very short TTL window (24 hours or less) with strict access controls and audit logging.  
- Residency: EU-only processing for the inference layer; metadata-only analytics can be US but must be pseudonymized.  
- Evidence: they’ll need SOC 2 summary and a short mapping of what data we persist and for how long.

Our proposed approach:  
1) Offer an initial pilot that runs on Redwood Private in their EU VPC region with a 24-hour ephemeral KV + optional 0-retention profile for selected routes.  
2) Provide a compact evidence package (SOC 2 summary + config playbook) and a proposed contract clause for a short-log exception covering the pilot.  
3) If pilot proves safe for a chosen workload, we’ll scope a 0-retention rollout for additional routes with the same constraints (no searchable logs, access via documented SOC/evidence lane).

Attachments: SOC2-Summary.pdf (high level) and a short Playbook: proposed-map-0to24h.docx.

Next steps / owners:  
- Sofia: share the SOC2 summary + playbook today (attached).  
- Lara / CloudVera: confirm which API routes you'd like 0-retention for (suggest start with the clinician assistant route).  
- Ben: once we have the routes, prepare the pilot runbook and a guarded config for 0-retention (no KV dumps, restricted access).

Timing: aim to get route list by EOD Friday so we can scope dev work next week.

Thanks — happy to hop on another call if you want to walk through specifics.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: SOC2-Summary.pdf (PDF)]
[Attachment: proposed-map-0to24h.docx (DOCX)]

From: Lara Mitchell <lara@cloudverahealth.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-29T11:04:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-call: Slim log / short-retention options and next steps

Hi Sofia — thanks for the clear recap and attachments. Quick clarifications from our security team before we lock the pilot routes:  
1) When you say "0-retention profile", do you mean absolutely no KV disk persistence (RAM-only cache) and no async archival in object storage?  2) For the 24-hour option, can you provide the exact fields that would be written to logs vs what we can redact at the agent layer?  
The routes we are thinking about initially: clinician-assistant.v1 and batch-summarize.v2 (the latter is lower risk but we want the same guarantees). We’ll confirm by Friday.

If you can get Ben to outline what controls prevent accidental dump/access (roles, audit hooks, JIT key access) that would be great. Also our legal wants a short template clause for the pilot stating Redwood will not retain model inputs beyond the agreed TTL and will limit employee access to engineering on a documented need basis.

Thanks,
Lara Mitchell
Head of Product Security
CloudVera Health

On Thu, Apr 29, 2027 at 09:12 Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Hi Lara — thanks again for the quick call this morning. Wanted to capture the main points and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned.
>

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Lara Mitchell <lara@cloudverahealth.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-29T16:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-call: Slim log / short-retention options and next steps

Hi Lara — Ben here, security/sales engineering. Short answers and controls summary below.

1) 0-retention profile: yes — for the pilot we can configure an in-memory-only KV cache for selected model routes (RAM-only, no async snapshotting, no write-through to object storage). That will also disable any debug-level token logging for those routes.  
2) 24-hour option: persisted metadata will be limited to a small routing envelope (request_id, timestamp, route) and an encrypted pointer; payloads are redacted. We’ll produce a field map for redaction.  

Guardrails we’ll apply:  
- Role-based access (RBAC) for any engineering access; default is no human-access. Access requires an internal Jira ticket + audit entry.  
- Immutable audit trail: all admin access is logged to the customer-facing audit feed and retained per the agreed pilot window.  
- Key handling: keys for the pilot can be customer-managed (bring-your-own KMS/HSM) so Redwood cannot decrypt payloads outside the session.  
- Telemetry: operational traces will be sampled and pseudonymized; full request bodies will never be included.

I’ll attach a short controls checklist and a draft pilot clause for legal. If CloudVera wants, we can also run the pilot entirely in a Private VPC in the Amsterdam region to satisfy residency.

Next: Sofia will confirm routes; I’ll prepare the redaction field map and the clause for your counsel.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: slimlog-controls-checklist.pdf (PDF)]

From: Lara Mitchell <security@cloudverahealth.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-30T14:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-call: Slim log / short-retention options and next steps

Thanks — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. We’ll:  
- Confirm final route list (clinician-assistant.v1, batch-summarize.v2) by EOD tomorrow.  
- Share our counsel’s requested wording for a pilot clause; high-level ask is: "Redwood will not persist model inputs beyond the pilot TTL; any retained metadata will be limited to routing identifiers and timestamps; CloudVera-managed KMS for pilot encryption."  
We’re happy to proceed with the Amsterdam Private VPC pilot as discussed — please send the playbook and the redaction field map as separate docs so our security team can review. Also please include a very short runbook describing incident escalation if there’s an access event.

Appreciate the fast turnaround — speak soon.

Lara Mitchell
Head of Product Security
CloudVera Health
